answer: Persistent Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity must keep a stable behavioural signature across epochs, such as timing patterns and interaction graph shape; an onyx-like invariant scored by distance from prior epochs. An identity whose signature drifts beyond a threshold gets its reputation reset. This forces a sybil operator to sustain distinct, expensive histories for every fake identity, turning each extra identity into an opal of ongoing cost. A single mismatch and the fable of cheap duplication collapses.
